question: How does the yogin who abides in avipa become the cause of knowledge for others?
premises: The yogin abiding in avipa protects bound beings.
Recognized self-lordship makes him the cause of knowledge.
One made dependent on the power-wheel cannot awaken others.
inference: Abiding in avipa with recognized self-lordship makes the yogin the cause of knowledge, while dependence on the power-wheel prevents awakening others.
uncertainties: Some editorial markers and fused forms are retained as given.
plain_english: The verse says the yogin who abides in avipa protects beings and, through recognized self-lordship, becomes the cause of knowledge; another, made dependent on the power-wheel, cannot awaken others.
